Picture: On the palm-lined driveway of the long white villa by the sea, Askeladden walks up with his bulging tote bag over his shoulder and a crooked brass bicycle horn in his hand. In the tall glass door at the top of the steps, the Heiress stands in her lilac suit with her arms crossed and one sharp eyebrow raised. White clouds race across a bright spring sky over the glittering fjord.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Askeladden: A slim, lean young man of about twenty with a clever, narrow face, sharp dark eyes that notice everything, straight black eyebrows, a thin straight nose and a lopsided, knowing smile. His black hair is shaggy and uncombed and falls over his ears and forehead. He wears a brown hooded canvas jacket over an ochre hoodie, dark-grey jeans and worn brown trainers, and carries a patched brown tote bag over his shoulder.
- the Heiress: A quick-witted young woman of about twenty-five, slim and upright, with a lively oval face, sharp, arched dark eyebrows, bright amber eyes, a small pointed nose and a mouth always ready with a clever reply. Her glossy chestnut hair is piled up in a high bun held by a slim silver clip. She wears a sharply tailored lilac trouser suit over a white silk top, small silver earrings and pointed silver-grey heels.

Story world: Present-day Norway. The Tycoon's villa stands by the sea: a long, white modernist house of glass and concrete with a driveway lined with tall potted palms, a wide lawn, a gleaming white kitchen with a marble counter that nobody has ever cooked on, a huge living room with a thick pale carpet, and a marble foyer with tall glass doors facing the fjord, overlooked by an open gallery. Askeladden's finds are a black zip tie, a shard of a white saucer wrapped in a paper napkin, a dead magpie, two crooked old brass bicycle horns with black rubber bulbs that look exactly alike, and an old, worn-out shoe sole with a hole right through it. He carries them in a patched brown tote bag.

This story's season, light and colours: A bright, windy spring day by the sea: racing white clouds, a glittering blue-grey fjord and fresh yellow-green lawns and birches along the road. Inside the villa: cool white marble, glass and pale stone, with the lilac of her suit and the warm brass of the horns as the only strong colours.

Art style: Contemporary Scandinavian editorial illustration: flat, graphic shapes with subtle risograph grain and a little hand-drawn texture, clean confident lines and a limited palette of spot inks led by deep petrol blue, with fjord teal, lingonberry red, honey mustard, sage green, warm paper off-white and ink charcoal, like the pages of a risograph-printed book, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, in the cool, clear Nordic light of today. Present-day Norway: fjord towns, suburbs, farms with tractors, cabins, ferries, roadside petrol stations, offices and flats, grey rain and bright snow, with people in modern clothes such as rain jackets, knitted sweaters, hoodies, suits and work wear. The magic of the tale appears plainly in this everyday world: trolls, talking animals and enchantments look real and slightly absurd, drawn in the same flat style. Every character has their own face, build, age, hair and clothes exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Dry humour, careful composition with one focal point and plenty of negative space. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

illustrations.anchor: Han tok bussen og gikk det siste stykket.
illustrations.caption: Ti meter lenger borte lå maken til det. Askeladden tok med alt.
illustrations.alt: Askeladden sitter på huk i veikanten og plukker opp et gammelt sykkelhorn av messing. Maken holder han i den andre hånda, og i veska har han en strips, et skår og en skjære.

illustrations.caption: Hun svarte ikke. Men hun lukket glassdøra.
illustrations.alt: I foajeen lukker dattera glassdøra igjen uten å si et ord. Askeladden står foran henne med en utslitt skosåle, og oppe på galleriet setter faren fra seg kaffekoppen.
illustrations.prompt: In the marble foyer of the villa, the Heiress, speechless for the first time in her life, her lips pressed together, pulls the tall glass door shut again with the glittering fjord behind it. Askeladden stands before her holding an old, worn-out shoe sole with a hole right through it and a calm, lopsided smile. Up on the open gallery above them, the Tycoon slowly sets down his coffee cup.
